name: multi_timeframe_confirmation_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, large institutional directional orders (FII/DII TWAP programs) sustain price above both the 5-minute and 15-minute EMA throughout the execution window — visible as EMA(60) > EMA(180) alignment at 5-second bars. Within these institutional trends, retail stop-loss cascades and counter-trend scalpers create 30-90 second micro-pullbacks that temporarily drive the 1-minute RSI below 30. At the moment RSI crosses back above the oversold threshold, the counter-trend flow is exhausted and the institutional bid reasserts. At 5-second resolution we can detect this RSI crossing in real time and enter before the first 5-10 spot points of trend resumption — the original 1-minute bars could only confirm the pullback was ending after it had already run half its course.

indicators.name: ema_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute fast EMA — context filter for 5-min institutional trend direction. NOT a 12x blind scaling of the original EMA_9_5min; instead we preserve the same 5-minute TIME window since that is the relevant order flow accumulation window for institutional TWAP programs. 60 bars × 5s = exactly 5 min.

indicators.name: ema_180
indicators.purpose: 15-minute slow EMA — dominant trend context filter. NOT 12x of the original EMA_21_5min (which would give 252 bars = 21 min). Chosen as 15 min (180 bars) to give a 3:1 ratio with the fast EMA (same directional logic as 9:21 = ~2.3x in the original but rounded to a cleaner 15-min window). Context filters can use longer lookbacks — this is NOT a trade trigger.

indicators.name: rsi_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute RSI for micro-pullback detection — trade trigger. 12 bars × 5s = 60s = exactly 1 minute. The original used RSI(7) on 1-min bars to detect 7-minute pullback cycles. We use RSI(12) at 5-second bars because we want to detect the SAME 1-minute pullback pattern (not a 7-minute one). 7 × 12 = 84 bars would capture 7-minute cycles — far too long for a 15-90 second hold. RSI(12) at 5s detects the exact 1-min oscillation that represents the micro-pullback within the 5-min trend.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.purpose: Session cumulative VWAP — directional confirmation filter. Cumulative from session open; no time-scaling needed. VWAP acts as the institutional participation benchmark: if close > VWAP and EMA trend is up, institutional flow dominates the buy side, confirming the RSI pullback is a dip-to-buy rather than a trend reversal.

conditions: rsi_12 crosses from below 30 to above 30 (1-min micro-pullback ending, confirmation bar)
close > vwap (price above institutional benchmark — institutional buy side dominant)
buy_ce.confirmation: RSI(12) crossing above oversold threshold on the signal bar itself

conditions: rsi_12 crosses from above 70 to below 70 (1-min micro-rally exhaustion, confirmation bar)
close < vwap (price below institutional benchmark — institutional sell side dominant)
buy_pe.confirmation: RSI(12) crossing below overbought threshold on the signal bar itself

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option pts because a valid micro-pullback entry in a 5-min NIFTY uptrend should not retrace more than 6 spot points after RSI crosses back up (3 pts at delta ~0.5). If it does, the micro-pullback is continuing into a deeper reversal of the 5-min trend — the thesis is wrong. This is the tightest calibration for the 15-30s expected hold at 3-bar timescale (NIFTY typical: 1-3 pts in 15s).
exit.target_rationale: 5 option pts = ~10 spot points. A micro-trend resumption after RSI oversold recovery in a confirmed 5-min NIFTY uptrend typically extends 10-20 spot points within the next 30-90 seconds. Targeting the lower end (10 pts = 5 option pts at delta 0.5) gives 1:1.67 R:R with high probability of being hit within the 90-second max hold. Calibrated against typical 1-minute NIFTY move of 3-7 pts.

filters.vix_filter: none — strategy trades the index trend direction which is defined at all VIX levels; RSI extremes naturally compress in trending high-VIX environments providing a natural self-filter
filters.time_filter: 09:25-15:20 IST (skip first 10 min for EMA warmup; no late-day choppy close)
filters.volume_filter: none — index volume is noisy at 5s; RSI level already filters low-momentum bars
filters.trend_filter: EMA_60 vs EMA_180 crossover is the primary trend filter
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close prices; no spread cost in model

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — multi-timeframe EMA alignment reflects genuine institutional order flow persistence; RSI crossing logic is robust and self-adaptive to session volatility

adaptation_notes: Key changes from original: (1) Stock universe → single NIFTY index: original traded top-30 FnO stocks; we trade NIFTY which is smoother, more liquid, and driven by institutional flow rather than per-stock events. (2) Timeframe compression: EMA lookbacks changed from 9/21 on 5-min bars (45/105 min) to 60/180 bars at 5s (5/15 min) — NOT 12x scaling but explicit time-window matching. (3) Entry trigger RSI: original used RSI(7) on 1-min bars; we use RSI(12) on 5s bars to capture the SAME 1-minute pullback cycle, not a 7-minute one. (4) Removed trailing stop and signal exit — too complex for 15-90 second holds. (5) ATR-based stops replaced with fixed option premium points calibrated to NIFTY's typical micro-move magnitudes. (6) Removed stock-specific filters (earnings filter, spread filter based on equity bid-ask).
weaknesses: 5-min EMA lag: by the time EMA(60) > EMA(180) on NIFTY, the first 5-min trend leg may be mostly done — entering on the 2nd pullback instead of the 1st
RSI(12) at 5s can spike below 30 even in strong uptrends on a single large candle, creating false pullback signals
VWAP confirmation adds a filter that disqualifies early-session entries when price has not yet moved relative to VWAP
Strategy does not fire in range-bound sessions where EMA crossover never develops — 3-4 days/month may produce zero signals
At 5-second resolution, RSI crossing logic fires on very short bursts that may reverse within 1-2 bars; position management relies entirely on the time stop
